svg.text: D-A TWIN TURRET — two rods through a disc-in-disc ceiling
Only two smooth rods hang into the wet cell. Turning two flush discs moves each rod anywhere in a circle; all motors sit in the dry room above.
outer disc Ø470, inner Ø240, e = 117 → reach Ø468
rod Ø40, Z 400, 200 N, yaw 15 Nm 0–300 rpm
11 servo axes, all in dry rooms
DRY DRIVE ROOM (Zone N): disc motors, Z screws, yaw motors
TOP VIEW of the cell: disc angles = rod position
outer disc Ø470 turns in the ceiling (seal S1)
inner disc Ø240, set 117 off-centre (seal S2)
rod Ø40, 117 off the inner centre (seal S3)
All seal lines are circles; the two rods together are
also a parallel gripper (0–900 mm, 100 N) for pots and boxes.
weak points: two Ø470 seams above open food; a wet rod
sliding into the dry room; about 30 utensil skills to tune

g.text: 1/6 Two discs in the ceiling turn: each rod reaches any point of a Ø468 circle — a SCARA made of flush plates.
2/6 Pick-up without a gripper: the rod pushes into the utensil's bayonet socket and twists (Z + yaw).
3/6 Carry hand presses a comb onto the onion; the blade cuts between the tines. The board's load cells feel each cut.
4/6 Planetary mixer: the inner disc spins so the hook orbits in the bowl, while yaw turns the hook.
5/6 Every retraction washes the rod: ring nozzle, scraper and drained lantern in the ceiling collar.
6/6 The carry hand is also the spray lance: it hoses the ceiling, walls, docks and the other rod.
